seoPage.title: Do EV Batteries Die Quickly? Myth vs Reality | EVSavari
seoPage.metaDescription: Do EV Batteries Die Quickly? Myth vs Reality — practical ownership guidance for Indian buyers.
seoPage.intro: The myth: EV batteries become useless within a few years. The reality: packs age gradually; warranties and habits matter more than viral anecdotes.

editorialSections.title: The myth
paragraphs: You may hear that all EV batteries ‘die’ after three years. That generalisation ignores warranty terms, climate, and how the car is charged.

editorialSections.title: Practical reality
bullets: Gradual capacity loss is normal — it is not usually sudden total failure.
Manufacturers publish warranty thresholds — read your variant’s document.
Heat and frequent unnecessary DC fast charging can accelerate wear.

editorialSections.title: Limitations to accept
paragraphs: A 8–10 year old EV may suit low km buyers differently than a heavy highway user — inspect used packs carefully.

misconceptions.myth: All packs fail at the same rate
misconceptions.reality: Chemistry, thermal management, and usage differ by model.
Software manages health — physical ageing still occurs.

editorialSections.title: Beginner guidance
bullets: Track your weekly km before buying kWh you will never use.
Ask the dealer for warranty transfer rules on used EVs.

faq.question: Will my battery die in three years?
faq.answer: Unlikely as a sudden total failure — plan for gradual range change over years.

faq.question: Does fast charging ruin batteries?
faq.answer: Occasional DC is fine for many owners — constant fast charging without need may add stress.

faq.question: What does warranty usually cover?
faq.answer: Capacity or defect thresholds for a period — terms vary by brand.

faq.question: Used EV risk?
faq.answer: Request service history and a drive that matches your km needs.

faq.question: Next step?
faq.answer: Compare battery sizes only after your commute pattern is clear.
